question: ‘Why I am an Atheist’ is an autobiography of whom among the following Revolutionaries?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhagat Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bhagat Singh was a prominent Indian revolutionary who played a pivotal role in the Indian independence movement against British colonial rule.
 
• He was born on September 28, 1907, in Banga, Punjab, British India (now in Pakistan).
 
• His essay "Why I am an Atheist" was written in 1930 while he was imprisoned in Lahore Central Jail.
 
• In this essay, Bhagat Singh articulates his rationalist and atheistic beliefs, challenging religious dogmas and advocating for a more scientific and humanistic approach to life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandrashekhar Azad**

 
 
• He was another prominent Indian revolutionary who reorganized the Hindustan Republican Association under its new name of Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) after the death of its founder, Ram Prasad Bismil.
 
• He was involved in several revolutionary activities against the British government, including the Kakori Train Robbery in 1925.
 
• Azad was known for his fearless attitude and commitment to the cause of Indian independence.
 
• He died on February 27, 1931, in a gunfight with the police at Alfred Park in Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Suryakant Sen**
 
 
• Suryakant Sen was not a prominent figure in the Indian independence movement, and there is little historical information available about him in the context of Indian revolutionary activities.
 
• His mention in the options might be a distractor or an error.
 
 
 
• **Ramprasad Bismil**
 
 
• He was a renowned Indian revolutionary who participated in the Mainpuri Conspiracy of 1918 and the Kakori Train Robbery in 1925.
 
• He was also a poet and writer, known for his patriotic compositions.
 
• Bismil was a founder member of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA), which aimed at overthrowing British rule in India through armed struggle.
 
• He was executed by the British authorities on December 19, 1927.
